arxiv-2103-06655.title: The speed of breaking waves controls sea surface drag
arxiv-2103-06655.creator: Alex Ayet 1,2, Bertrand Chapron 1, Peter Sutherland 1, Gabriel G. Katul 3
arxiv-2103-06655.description: Abstract The coupling between wind-waves and atmospheric surface layer turbulence sets surface drag. This coupling is however usually represented through a roughness length. Originally suggested on purely dimensional grounds, this roughness length does not directly correspond to a measurable physical quantity of the wind-and-wave system.

arxiv-2109-07364.title: Towards Incremental Transformers: An Empirical Analysis of Transformer Models for Incremental NLU
arxiv-2109-07364.creator: Patrick Kahardipraja Brielen Madureira David Schlangen
arxiv-2109-07364.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Patrick Kahardipraja Brielen Madureira David Schlangen. Incremental processing allows interactive systems to respond based on partial inputs, which is a desirable property e.g. The currently popular Transformer architecture inherently processes sequences as a whole, abstracting away the notion of time. Recent work attempts to apply Transformers incrementally via restart-incrementality by repeatedly feeding, to an unchanged model, increasingly longer input prefixes to produce partial outputs. However, this approach is computationally costly and does not scale efficiently for long sequences.

arxiv-2310-15833.title: The positional probability and true host star identification of TESS exoplanet candidates 2023 The positional probability and true host star identification of TESS exoplanet candidates – References
arxiv-2310-15833.creator: Andreas Hadjigeorghiou, David J. Armstrong
arxiv-2310-15833.description: Abstract We present a method for deriving a probabilistic estimate of the true source of a detected TESS transiting event. Our method relies on comparing the observed photometric centroid offset for the target star with models of the offset that would occur if the event was either on the target or any of the Gaia identified nearby sources.

arxiv-2401-13034.title: Locality Sensitive Sparse Encoding for Learning World Models Online
arxiv-2401-13034.creator: Zichen Liu, Chao Du, Wee Sun Lee, Min Lin
arxiv-2401-13034.description: Abstract Acquiring an accurate world model online for model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) is challenging due to data nonstationarity, which typically causes catastrophic forgetting for neural networks (NNs). From the online learning perspective, a Follow-The-Leader (FTL) world model is desirable, which optimally fits all previous experiences at each round.

arxiv-2402-10555.title: SPAR: Personalized Content-Based Recommendation via Long Engagement Attention
arxiv-2402-10555.creator: Chiyu Zhang Yifei Sun Jun Chen Jie Lei Muhammad Abdul-Mageed, Sinong Wang Rong Jin Sem Park Ning Yao Bo Long
arxiv-2402-10555.description: Abstract Leveraging users’ long engagement histories is essential for personalized content recommendations. The success of pretrained language models (PLMs) in NLP has led to their use in encoding user histories and candidate items, framing content recommendations as textual semantic matching tasks. However, existing works still struggle with processing very long user historical text and insufficient user-item interaction.

arxiv-2408-00552.creator: Mustafa Goksu Ozlu, Vahagn Mkhitaryan, Colton B. Fruhling, Alexandra Boltasseva, Vladimir M. Shalaev
arxiv-2408-00552.description: Abstract In this study, we investigate the dynamics of dispersive photonic time crystals (PTCs) and their potential applications for controlling light-matter interaction. arxiv-2601-04555.title: Improving Semi-Supervised Contrastive Learning via Entropy-Weighted Confidence Integration of Anchor-Positive Pairs
arxiv-2601-04555.creator: Shogo Nakayama, Masahiro Okuda
arxiv-2601-04555.description:
A 2026 arXiv research paper by Shogo Nakayama, Masahiro Okuda. Abstract

Conventional semi-supervised contrastive learning methods assign pseudo-labels only to samples whose highest predicted class probability exceeds a predefined threshold, and then perform supervised contrastive learning using those selected samples. In this study, we propose a novel loss function that estimates the confidence of each sample based on the entropy of its predicted probability distribution and applies confidence-based adaptive weighting.

pmc-10625663.creator: Mohammed Khaleel I.KH. Almadhoun, Abdallah Wasel Hattab, Nemer Nedal Alazzeh, Sufyan Taleb Aladwan, Osamah Ta’amneh
pmc-10625663.description: Dandy-Walker Syndrome (DWS) is a rare congenital neurological condition characterized by cerebellar and posterior fossa malformations, often presenting a variable clinical spectrum. Common complications include hydrocephalus, necessitating interventions like ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunts, and endoscopic third ventriculostomy (ETV). We describe the case of a five-month-old infant conceived through in vitro fertilization (IVF), initially presenting with cold-like symptoms, later diagnosed with DWS.

pmc-12698360.creator: Jun-Young Kim, Nitesh Gahlot, Hyung Bin Park
pmc-12698360.description: Frozen shoulder (FS) is a challenging disorder defined by persistent shoulder pain and progressively reduced joint motion.
